body.note: Translucent at 95% opacity; ramp derived from the opaque #eae8f5.

body-solid.note: The body lavender with no translucency, for windows on the desktop (setup).

rule.note: Frame Navy at 20%: the hairline between parts of a window. Ramp from the opaque #3e527c.

inset-bg.note: White at 55% over the lavender body: the route box and the suggestions.

inset-edge.note: Frame Navy at 30%, edging an inset box. Ramp from the opaque #3e527c.

edit.note: Focus ring in every window, the dashed drag box, checkbox accent, and at 8% the row hover tint.

veil.note: 30% navy over the whole title-marking window; non-zero so every pixel takes the mouse. Ramp from the opaque #121c38.

gradients.name: bar
gradients.purpose: The --bar custom property: every title bar (overlay, search view and setup), the collapsed icon, setup's mark icon and the read test reads.

gradients.name: button
gradients.purpose: --button: setup's primary button and the overlay's deep-steel icon buttons at rest.

gradients.name: button-hover
gradients.purpose: --button-hover: a deep-steel button hovered or pressed.

gradients.name: button-light
gradients.purpose: --button-light: secondary and light icon buttons at rest and pressed.

headline.purpose: The Map Name in white with a navy outline, in the overlay and setup's recognised test read; wraps to two lines. An unread status takes the slot at 15px in plain ink. Time to Level and setup step headings use 18px bold in plain ink.

street.purpose: Above the Map Name, the minimap's own idiom; also setup's step count.

title.purpose: Section headings (Hidden Portals, Mobs, the Hunting Target's mob), destinations, summary, rate and target values. 14px in Street Navy for the search view's title and setup's window name.

body-reading.purpose: Setup prose, the search field, and the title-marking hint's heading (bold there): read at rest, one step larger than the overlay.

body.purpose: Notes, the mob and rates tables, the suggestions; tabular figures throughout.

body-small.purpose: Positions, labels, units, table headers, the route, candidate rows, key hints, the crawl note, footer.

button.purpose: Setup button labels, sentence case (12px on the Overlay guide button).

label.purpose: Tags and the doubt chip (uppercase only on the chip). The 9px Time to Level badge is an exception below this step.

shadows.name: window-inner-highlight
shadows.purpose: Inside the panel frame and the title-marking hint; 0.7 on the collapsed icon and setup's mark icon.

shadows.name: bar-top-highlight
shadows.purpose: Top edge of every title bar and the recognised test read; 0.55 on the doubt chip, 0.3 on deep-steel buttons (primary and icon), solid #fff on light steel.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: A held deep-steel button; 0.25 on light steel. Buttons sink, never lift.

shadows.name: field-inset
shadows.purpose: The search field, the one surface set into the body.

shadows.name: glyph-ring
shadows.purpose: Dark edge on mob dots (mob-edge) and orange dots (orange-deep); the alert dot adds 0 0 0 2px #fff.

shadows.name: lettering-outline
shadows.value: -1px -1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 0 -1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 1px -1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), -1px 0 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 1px 0 0 var(--outline, #22325a), -1px 1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 0 1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 1px 1px 0 var(--outline, #22325a), 0 2px 2px rgba(20, 30, 60, 0.35)
shadows.purpose: The shared --lettering text-shadow: eight 1px offsets in outline plus 0 2px 2px rgba(20, 30, 60, 0.35). Map Names only.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus (:focus-visible) on every button and the search field, in the overlay and setup. Not a shadow; recorded here because the component schema cannot hold it.

tints.name: row-hover
tints.purpose: Edit Blue at 8%: suggestion and result rows under the pointer. A literal in styles.css, not a custom property.

narrative.northStar: The Window the Game Forgot to Ship
narrative.overview:
The overlay sits beside the game's own windows (the Quest Helper, the minimap) and is made from their materials: a translucent lavender-grey body, a steel-periwinkle title bar with a white top highlight and a dark-navy hairline, the map name in white bold lettering outlined in navy the way the minimap draws it, the minimap's legend of blue portal rings and red mob dots, and the game's small steel window buttons. The game supplies the materials and one signature move. Organisation, hierarchy and density come from a working tool: EXP pace first when it is tracked, then hidden exits, then the mobs, then the way to the Hunting Target, then the credit. It is not a screenshot of a game window. The setup window and the title-marking window are built from the same materials, so every MapleCompass window reads as one more game window.

It is light because the game's windows are light, and dense because it is read in glances between attacks. Every state is drawn in the same window. Doubt and problems get the game's orange, and nothing else does. The confirmed rejection is the generic dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top, which this world replaced.

Every window takes the pointer. The overlay is always clickable, but a click never takes the keyboard from the game except in the search view, where the query field needs it. The panel is dragged by its title bar when it sits inside the game or is detached. Its buttons (deep steel in the title bar, light steel in the body) and setup's buttons carry the game's hover, pressed and keyboard-focus states; list rows in the search view take a faint hover tint. Its height follows its content. Nothing in any window moves: there is no transition or animation anywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Light window body in the game's lavender (translucent over the game, opaque on the desktop), under a gradient steel-blue title bar.
Map name in outlined white lettering, with the Street Name above it as on the minimap.
Two icon vocabularies only: minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, mini-minimap) in CSS and SVG, and drawn line icons on the game's small steel buttons.
Game orange appears only for doubt and problems.
One plain bold sans (Arial) throughout; tabular figures in the overlay.
Buttons in every window have the game's hover, pressed and focus states. No motion anywhere.

rules.name: The Orange Means Doubt Rule
rules.body: Game orange marks only uncertainty and problems: the "Not sure" chip, problem notes, the collapsed alert dot. A confirmed state never uses it, so orange can't become decoration. Search tiers are told apart by weight and ink, never by orange.

rules.name: The Minimap Legend Rule
rules.body: Portal blue and mob red come from the minimap's legend and keep that meaning. Blue is for portals and red is for mobs, with no other uses.

rules.name: The Over the Game, Translucent Rule
rules.body: A window laid over the game uses the translucent Window Lavender (body); a window on the desktop uses the opaque one (body-solid). Same colour, different footing.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: In the overlay all figures are tabular (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the body), and numeric columns are right-aligned so EXP, HP, rates and share line up from one glance to the next.

rules.name: The Outlined Lettering Rule
rules.body: Only a Map Name uses white lettering with a navy outline (the shared `--lettering` text-shadow: a 1px stroke in eight directions plus one soft 0 2px 2px drop). It appears in the overlay title bar and in setup's recognised test read, nowhere else. Everything else, Time to Level included, is ink on the lavender body.

rules.name: The Notes Wrap, Names Truncate Rule
rules.body: Notes and the Map Name wrap so they can be read in full. Single-line facts (destinations, mob names, route stops, suggestion names, result maps) truncate with an ellipsis instead of growing the panel.

rules.name: The Chrome, Not Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn the way the game draws it, with highlights and hairlines. Nothing floats on a blurred drop shadow.

dos: **Do** build new states and windows from the game's window materials: the Window Lavender body, the Title Bar Steel gradient with its white highlight and hairline, and navy ink.
**Do** use the translucent body for windows over the game and the opaque body for windows on the desktop.
**Do** reserve game orange for doubt and problems, and pair it with words and a shape (chip, dot, bordered note) so the state never relies on colour alone.
**Do** draw icons as minimap glyphs (portal ring, mob dot, mini-minimap) in CSS or inline SVG, or as 1.8-stroke line icons on the game's small steel buttons.
**Do** keep overlay figures tabular and numeric columns right-aligned.
**Do** let notes and the Map Name wrap, and truncate single-line facts with an ellipsis.
**Do** keep the Street Name above the Map Name wherever a map is shown as the overlay shows it.

**Do** give every button, in every window, hover, pressed and a 2px Edit Blue `:focus-visible` ring offset 2px, deep steel where it acts from a title bar or moves setup forward and light steel beside it or in a body.
**Do** mark a selected row with Selection Periwinkle and its inset edge, and set a list into the body as an inset box.
donts: **Don't** return to the dark dev-tools card with a stats table on top.
**Don't** use orange, or the outlined white lettering, for anything other than their single roles.
**Don't** add small labels or kickers above content beyond the Street Name in the title bar; a label belongs only to the field or figure it names.
**Don't** let a click on the overlay take the keyboard from the game outside the search view.
**Don't** add motion (transitions or animations) to any window.
**Don't** float any window on a blurred drop shadow; depth is inset highlights and hairlines.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or icon fonts.
